gallery.title: File:Plutarch and herm.jpg
gallery.description:
Left: Bust of Plutarch or of another Neoplatonic philosopher.
Right: Headless herm of a votive with the bust of Plutarch, set up by the people of Delphi around 125 AD.
The inscription on the herm reads:

ΔΕΛΦΟΙ ΧΑΙΡΩΝΕΥΣΙ ΝΟΜΟΥ
ΠΛΟΥΤΑΡΧΟΝ ΕΘΗΚΑΝ
ΤΟΙΣ ΑΜΦΙΚΤΙΟΝΩΝ
ΔΕΛΦΟΙΣ ΠΕΙΘΟΜΕΝΟΙ
The engraved inscription on the marble pillar reveals that this votive with the bust of Plutarch was set up by the people of Delphi and the citizens of Chearonea in honour of the great author and priest of Apollo. 

Both items were found near the southeast corner of the temple of Apollo at Delphi.

gallery.filename: Plutarch stele inscription 100 AD, AM of Delphi 4070060092.jpg
gallery.title: File:Plutarch stele inscription 100 AD, AM of Delphi 4070060092.jpg
gallery.source: Plutarch stele inscription 100 AD, AM of Delphi 4070060092
gallery.description:
Stela of Plutarch, circa 100 AD. Detail of the inscription that reads:
ΔΕΛΦΟΙ ΧΑΙΡΩΝΕΥΣΙΝ ΟΜΟΥ
ΠΛΟΥΤΑΡΧΟΝ ΕΘΗΚΑΝ
ΤΟΙΣ ΑΜΦΙΚΤΥΟΝΩΝ
ΔΟΓΜΑΣΙ ΠΕΙΘΟΜΕΝΟΙ
("The Delphians, along with the Chaeroneans, dedicated this (image of) Plutarch, following the precepts of the Amphictyony")
The engraved inscription on the marble pillar reveals that this votive with the bust of Plutarch was set up by the people of Delphi and the citizens of Chearonea in honour of the author and priest of Apollo.

Name of Plutarch is very easy to read at the beginning of the second line (in the accusative: PLOYTARCHON). Archaeological Museum of Delphi, N 4070.
